objective: Systematically optimize the existing SM90 FP8-activation x OCP-MXFP4-weight persistent MegaMoE kernel on exactly 4x NVIDIA H20 for the exact DeepSeek-V4-Flash model shape. The verified live starting point passes exact correctness but is slower than the same-process live FP8 baseline at every M: minimum speedup 0.433963x and geometric mean 0.653225x over M=8..8192, with the worst discontinuity at M=512 (895.7us FP8 versus 2064.0us MXFP4). First isolate and repair the M=512 tuning transition, while separately searching equivalence-tested Humming-style DP4A/PRMT E2M1+E8M0 register decode and small-M BN512/BK64 scheduling mechanisms informed by generated SASS. Achieve every-row speedup at least 1.05x and geometric-mean speedup at least 1.10x versus live FP8 without weakening the real four-rank distributed workload, and preserve the real eight-rank path for its separate campaign.
fixed_constraints: The workload is exactly DeepSeek-V4-Flash: hidden=4096, intermediate_hidden=2048, num_experts=256, topk=6, world_size=4, FP8 activations, OCP E2M1+E8M0 group-size-32 MXFP4 routed weights, SwiGLU, activation_clamp=10, fast_math=1.
MegaMoE performance evidence must come from one real four-GPU H20 run. Never use or rank a single-GPU timing, and never assemble ranks across hosts.
Evaluate every M in 8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192; never substitute the MiMo 6144/2048/384/topk8 defaults.
Every candidate must pass exact-dequantized MXFP4 correctness before performance is comparable; do not loosen any FP4 tolerance or cosine/norm gate.

Use same-process same-input interleaved CUPTI cold-L2 measurements against the live FP8 path. PR #383 published numbers have no equivalent four-rank denominator and must not be used for ranking this campaign.
The success gate is every-row speedup >=1.05 and geometric-mean speedup >=1.10 versus live FP8; optimize the minimum row first.

The verified starting baseline is min=0.433963x and geomean=0.653225x. M=512 is the first structural priority: FP8=895.7us, MXFP4=2064.0us. Other MXFP4 times in M order are 446.6,660.7,830.1,897.0,935.0,938.8,2064.0,2104.0,4120.0,7397.0,13434.0us.

Retain this causal prior from the complete real-world4 v2 measurement even though its old artifact-path bug prevented a sealed receipt: assigning M=512 the exact M<=256 tuple {BM64, BN256, experts_per_wave=48, stages=3, smem_capacity=209856, swap_ab=false, mode2=true, quad_ilp=false} produced FP8=897.8us, MXFP4=956.8us, M512 speedup=0.938336x, global minimum=0.560040x, and geomean=0.709343x. Wave-2 evidence separately shows that BM64/BN256/stage3 with experts_per_wave=64 and the default SMEM cap does not reproduce the gain (M512=2072.0us). Requalify the exact positive tuple under the repaired receipt protocol before exploring further variants.
Do not use CUDA graphs, framework fallbacks, pre-expanded persistent FP8 weight copies, benchmark shortcuts, exact-output caches, skipped synchronization, or altered inputs.
Preserve the public Python/C++ ABI, actual SymBuffer<4> distributed protocol, packed Mode2 Braided MXFP4 layout, real dispatch/communication/scatter, and one persistent kernel launch.

Do not break the separate SymBuffer<8> path. Run the template compile gate for both four and eight ranks after structural changes even though performance evaluation in this campaign is four-rank only.
Use Humming and Marlin as mechanism/SASS references, not performance denominators. Preserve Hopper QGMMA, E8M0 group width 32, saturation/underflow semantics, and the distributed persistent protocol.

Keep experimental axes attributable. Start with two isolated lanes: (1) diagnose and repair the M=512 tile/stage/experts-per-wave transition; (2) Humming DP4A/PRMT decode plus small-M BN512/BK64 only when exact equivalence is demonstrated. Do not mix arithmetic, tiling, cache policy, and barriers in one candidate.
NCU counters are unavailable due ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM; do not invent counter evidence. Use generated SASS, register/resource reports, timings, and controlled A/B changes.
Never kill or interfere with existing SGLang. Only use GPUs explicitly bound by CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES after verifying they are idle.

Every generated file must stay under the host-specific workspace root, including temporary files, SASS/cubin dumps, evaluation data, JIT caches, builds, logs, environments, and worktrees; do not use home or /tmp. On 10.6.131.5 and 10.6.131.6 the only allowed root is /lustre/raplab/client/jinyanc/workspace/jinyanc; on 10.6.131.24 and 10.6.131.25 the only allowed root is /raid/sharedspace/jinyanc.
Commit each correct measured improvement before starting the next risky experiment and keep changes within scope_paths.
